objects.meaning: Examine local medium-particle motion through a transverse elastic-cord wave; propagation is not the transport of every particle along the cord.
Mass and elasticity, cross-section elastic forces, net restoring force, inertial overshoot, deceleration and the maximum-displacement turning point are all retained.
objects.qualification: The restoring-motion description is read within the lesson's small-amplitude outgoing oscillatory-wave model, not as a law for arbitrary superpositions.

objects.meaning: Identical metal balls suspended on strings and much lighter connecting springs separate inertia from elastic coupling without claiming complete equivalence to a continuous cord.
Figure 69 object identity and its source position are preserved.
The source's number-only Figure 69 caption is retained/localized without inventing figure description.
Leftmost ball moves sideways in the horizontal plane; deformed spring pulls the next ball in the same transverse direction, with a delayed inertial response.
objects.qualification: Both languages explicitly limit the account to small amplitude before appreciable loss or reflection. No finite dead time for the first force response is asserted.

objects.meaning: Period T, hand or mechanical drive, successive second/third-ball phase lag, forced common driving frequency and outgoing transverse propagation are retained.
objects.qualification: Common frequency is after the initial transient and before reflected waves return; phase lag does not assert that every pair of balls always has distinct phase.

defects.exactText: A large thin plate moving normally can approximate such a wave.
defects.defect: In ordinary English, 'moving normally' primarily means moving in the usual manner. It leaves the source's oscillatory motion perpendicular to the plate implicit, even though the later sentence explicitly states the wave's normal propagation direction. This is a localized clarity defect, not a new contradictory physics claim.
defects.smallestRepair: Replace only this sentence with: A large thin plate oscillating perpendicular to its surface can approximate such a wave.
defects.proposedReplacement: A large thin plate oscillating perpendicular to its surface can approximate such a wave.
defects.repairScope: One English sentence; preserve the large plate, uniform/isotropic-medium assumptions, uniform driving, phase definition and edge-diffraction caveat.

defects.exactText: These forces drive the local oscillations.
defects.defect: The actual normalized flow splits a six-sentence shear explanation into 2/3/1. The final anaphoric mechanism sentence completes the preceding restoring-force explanation; it is neither an independent definition nor a separate contextual qualification. The source's coherent restoring-force-to-oscillation explanation therefore ends as an arbitrary singleton.

objects.meaning: Cord/string/rod axial propagation is retained as a one-dimensional approximation with either axial travel direction, not a claim of only one signed direction.
Continuous gas/liquid/solid media and transmission through local interactions are retained; multidirectional propagation depends on source and medium.
The source's transition to new propagation features is retained.

Outward spreading, stone-generated surface ripples in shared Figure 64, flux per unit area per second, decreasing flux/amplitude, Section 11 and spring/pendulum/local-particle energy examples are retained.
objects.qualification: Steady uniform outward spreading without added energy, fixed other conditions and small oscillations qualify amplitude-squared scaling. Water-surface ripples are not falsely called liquid-bulk spherical waves.

objects.meaning: Geometric spreading decreases amplitude without converting mechanical energy into internal energy; absorption is a separate mechanism.
Ideal plane-wave exception, large driven plate, equal contact amplitude/phase, propagation normal to plate, equal-phase wavefront definition, Figure 73 and finite-edge diffraction are present.

objects.meaning: Figure 73 identity is preserved.

Rays are normal to equal-phase fronts; plane-wave rays are parallel straight lines, and ray/energy propagation alignment is confined to the uniform isotropic ray model.
Ideal plane waves have no geometric dilution; lossless uniform amplitude is constant, while dissipation or finite-beam spreading can reduce amplitude.
Rod touching water and oscillating vertically produces approximately straight surface fronts, equal phase parallel to the rod away from its ends, and Figure 74.
objects.qualification: The surface-wave/plane-wave analogy is expressly not evidence of liquid-bulk shear propagation.

Uniform pulsation in a uniform isotropic medium yields source-centered spherical equal-phase fronts and outward radial rays; Figure 75 remains referenced.
Steady uniform lossless outward spherical power spreads over larger spheres; flux and amplitude fall with radius at fixed medium/frequency even without absorption.
objects.qualification: No inverse-radius formula or numerical example has been added to the card. The sentence that names geometric spreading and the opening model context are valid singleton exceptions.

objects.meaning: Transverse displacement, shear, layer shifts, no first-order volume change in small pure shear, and solid restoring forces driving local oscillations are retained.
Ordinary liquids/gases lack static shear stiffness and cannot carry bulk elastic shear waves in the stated model; shear-stiff solids can, with explicit footnote ①.
objects.qualification: The statement is not extended to all transverse phenomena, viscoelastic high-frequency responses or liquid-surface motion.

objects.meaning: Footnote ① remains a separate labeled explanatory prose object. It retains the surface exception and correctly allows vertical/horizontal particle motion with gravity and surface tension restoring the surface.
objects.qualification: Neither language claims that real liquid-surface waves are necessarily pure transverse waves or that their restoring force is bulk shear elasticity.

objects.meaning: Longitudinal displacement, solid compression/extension, fluid compression/rarefaction, Section 37 and bulk restoring response in solids/liquids/gases are retained.
objects.qualification: Fluid propagation does not require sustained tensile stress. 'All media' means the three material-medium classes under discussion, not a vacuum.

objects.meaning: In the usual isotropic elastic-rock model, P travels faster than S; same-earthquake P/S arrival delay can estimate source-station distance with suitable speeds and paths.
objects.qualification: This is not an unqualified claim for every anisotropic solid, every wave path or every earthquake record. A single-station delay does not uniquely locate the source.
